document.title: Make agent-user.test.ts pass under any umask
document.brief:
Owner asked for this on 2026-10-14. Keep it small enough to finish within an hour, and end with a pull request. The task is not done until the PR is open.

Problem: `api/tests/security/agent-user.test.ts` (in the `security` sub-suite) passes only under umask 022. Under umask 077, which Jevellan thread shells use and some runners may use too, 2 cases fail. A run on 2026-10-14 confirmed it: the suite went red under 077, and the same file passed 23/23 under a process-local umask 022 on Node 20.

Likely cause (verify it): the fixtures create files and folders with an explicit `mode` (for example `writeFileSync(..., { mode: 0o644 })` at lines ~323-328 and ~402-409, `mkdirSync(..., { mode: 0o755 })`). The umask masks those modes (0o644 becomes 0o600 under 077). Assertions that expect untouched entries to keep their fixture mode then fail, for example `expect(mode(outside)).toBe(0o755)` and `expect(mode(join(outside, 'secret.txt'))).toBe(0o644)`, and the fixture modes the code under test reads differ too. Some fixtures already follow `writeFileSync`/`mkdirSync` with `chmodSync`, but not all.

Fix:
- Make every fixture set its mode explicitly with `chmodSync` after creating the entry, so the setup is the same under any umask. Do not assert on umask-derived modes.
- If any failing assertion is about a mode the product code (the agent-user module the test covers, under `api/src/`) itself creates and relies on the ambient umask for, that is a security-relevant product bug. Set the mode explicitly in the product code, not in the test, and say so in the PR.
- Do not change the umask globally for the test run, and do not loosen the assertions on what the product code sets.

Verify:
- Run the file under both umasks, e.g. `(umask 022 && npx vitest run api/tests/security/agent-user.test.ts)` and `(umask 077 && npx vitest run api/tests/security/agent-user.test.ts)`, or through the repo's vitest config. Use Node 20.
- Then run `npm run test:suite -- security --unit`.
- Never run `mobile`, `expensive` or `npm run test:all`.

Docs: add a short "Recently fixed" entry to `docs/findings.md` (slug `agent-user-test-umask`): the cause, the fix, and proof under both umasks.

Report: the cause, whether product code changed, the two umask runs' results, the security sub-suite totals, and the PR link.

document.title: WhatsApp undo: refuse negated requests and keep documents edited since the save
document.brief:
The nightly code review of gongiskhan/ekoa-code (770e76b09..7a7b36831) found two P2 defects in the WhatsApp saved-file undo added by #239 (Arquivo saved-file links and undo). Both can trash a person's documents they meant to keep. Pull main first, then reproduce each one end to end (or as close as the WhatsApp seam allows: a test that drives the real `verifyAsk` -> `undoSave` path) before fixing, and confirm both still exist.

1. Negated or non-undo messages authorize the undo. `asksToUndo` (`api/src/whatsapp/archive-files.ts:126-128`) matches deletion words anywhere in the first line, with no check for negation and no check that the message asks for an undo. It returns true for 'não apagues esses ficheiros', 'não desfaças nada' and the plain statement 'os relatórios estão errados'. `verifyAsk` (`:457-459`) uses it as the authorization guard before `undoSave` switches to the person's principal and trashes items. So a wrong model tool call can delete saved documents against an explicit instruction to keep them. Checking that the text came from the current user does not prevent this. Fix: require an affirmative undo directive, reject negated deletion requests, and fail closed when unclear. Consider whether this should be a Judge question rather than a keyword predicate: per the repo's CLAUDE.md the Judge (`api/src/judge/`) is the only thing that decides what something means. If you keep a deterministic guard, it must stay strict (affirmative only, negation refused). Add guard tests with the three examples above plus affirmative ones ('desfaz', 'apaga o que guardaste').

2. Undo trashes edits the person made after the save. `undoSave` (`:463-484`) loads each document's current row and passes that row's `_rev` to `objects.trash`. That only protects against a concurrent edit after the lookup, not against edits made since the original save. A person can rename a WhatsApp-saved document or add notes, leave it in the same folder, and a later 'desfaz' within 24 hours trashes it: the age, provenance and parent checks all still pass, `object-service.patch` keeps the provenance and `object-service.trash` accepts the current revision. The reviewer showed it in memory with a renamed, annotated document at revision 7. Fix: store the revision each document had when the save being undone happened, use it for the conditional delete, and keep (do not trash) documents changed since that save. Report the kept ones to the person in the reply. Follow the existing pattern in `api/src/archive/agent-tools.ts`, whose undo receipt already avoids taking over later human edits. Reuse that mechanism rather than writing a second copy (Capability Contract Rule 1).

Tests: regression tests red on the old code for both defects. Run `npm run test:suite -- caixa arquivo --unit`, plus `security` because this is an authorization guard. Never run `mobile`, `expensive` or `npm run test:all`. Record both in `docs/findings.md` as recently fixed (cause, fix, proof). Update `docs/diagrams/` if the undo's data shape changes (a stored save revision), and add a `docs/decisions.md` entry if the guard moves to the Judge. Report: the reproduction of each defect, the fix, the tests, and the PR.

document.brief:
Close the open finding `chat-thinking-wedge-estate` in docs/findings.md of gongiskhan/ekoa-code (section "Open - 2026-10-08 the wedged-worker chat case still misses in the whole browser estate"). Pull main first and check the finding is still open and the spec not since changed.

The finding: `web/e2e/chat-thinking.spec.ts:130` (the wedged-worker case) failed once in a full-estate run (PR #119, head `90e36e4`) while 576 other cases passed. The mocked clock had moved past the 5-minute stuck-run deadline (page showed "A pensar... 5m 10s") but the TIMEOUT bubble did not appear within 10 s. It passes alone (6/6 with `--repeat-each=3`). Suspected, not shown: under estate load the guard's `getRun` request after the clock jump settles too late for the 10 s window. The product code involved is `web/components/chat/chat-runtime.tsx`.

Steps:
1. Reproduce the flake under load, not alone: run the `chat` sub-suite e2e (`npm run test:suite -- chat --e2e`) repeatedly and/or the spec with `--repeat-each` and high worker parallelism, capturing the Playwright trace and network log of a failing run. Do not change the guard or the wait before you have evidence of the cause.
2. Fix the real cause. If it is the test (wait condition racing the guard's request), make the spec wait on the deterministic signal (the `getRun` response or the state change), not a longer timeout. If it is the product (the guard can miss the deadline under load), fix `chat-runtime.tsx` and pin it with a test that is red on the old code.
3. Prove the fix: show the flake rate before (N failures in M repeated loaded runs) and after (0 in at least the same M).
4. Update the finding in docs/findings.md to fixed (move to a "Recently fixed" entry with cause, fix and proof).

Test discipline: run the `chat` sub-suite (`--e2e` plus `--unit` if product code changed). Never run `mobile`, `expensive` or `npm run test:all`. Zero console errors on dashboard specs. If no cause can be shown after a serious attempt, report the evidence gathered and leave the finding open with the updated next step rather than papering over it with a bigger timeout.

Report: the cause, the fix, the before/after flake numbers, and the PR.

findings.what: [P2] Reject negated requests before authorizing WhatsApp undo
findings.detail: asksToUndo matches deletion words anywhere in the first line without checking negation or whether they request an undo. The current implementation returns true for both 'não apagues esses ficheiros' and 'não desfaças nada', as well as the statement 'os relatórios estão errados'. verifyAsk uses this predicate as the authorization guard before undoSave switches to the person's principal and trashes items. Consequently an erroneous model tool call can delete saved documents despite an explicit instruction to keep them; checking that the text came from the current user does not prevent this. Require an affirmative undo directive, reject negated deletion requests, and add guard tests covering these examples.

findings.what: [P2] Bind undo to the saved revision so subsequent edits survive
findings.detail: undoSave loads each document's current row and passes that same row's _rev to objects.trash. This protects only against a concurrent edit after the lookup, not edits made since the original save. A person can rename a WhatsApp document or add notes, leave it in the original folder, and then have those edits trashed by a later 'desfaz' within 24 hours. The age, provenance and parent checks all still pass. An in-memory execution of the current seam with a renamed, annotated document at revision 7 returned it in trashed and supplied revision 7 as the person; object-service.patch preserves the provenance, and object-service.trash accepts that current revision. Persist the revision associated with the save being undone and use it for the conditional delete, keeping documents changed since that save. The existing archive/agent-tools.ts undo receipt already explicitly avoids adopting later human edits.
